$comment: P2 fix lane: author every gap slot in Spanish units 7-14. The lane's product is content/es/candidates/u07-u14.jsonl. This file records what the lane measured, what it is blocked on, and the two things it can hand any later authoring lane: an EXACT, corpus-independent allowed_lemmas window per (unit, lesson), and a verifier that reproduces G5's own reject order over a shard.
whyOwnedIsEmpty: An authoring lane owns no test. INV-PACK-06 is V1-V4 at 100%, INV-PACK-08 is V6, INV-PACK-10 is the no-repair-path scan over the generator; all three are asserted by tools/coursekit tests that p2-g5-g6-gapfill-language already owns (docs/owned/p2-g5-g6.json), and all three are measured over a BUILT pack. This lane turns them green by supplying the content those validators run on, not by adding a test. Claiming the ids here with a test that asserts a JSONL file parses would be the 'owning test that proves nothing' the plan's rule 4 is written against.

blocked.on: content/es/authoring/gap-brief.jsonl (lane p2fix-ledger-freeze) does not exist, and until G4 is fixed it cannot exist with a usable ledger.
blocked.rootCause: tools/coursekit/src/coursekit/stages/g4_select.py, the `if choice is None` branch, emitted EVERY gap row with `new_lemmas: []` and `known_lemmas: []` unconditionally. G5 computes `allowed = set(known_lemmas) | set(new_lemmas)`, so a gap slot's permitted vocabulary was the EMPTY SET. The only candidate that can pass the `stale_ledger` axis against such a row is one declaring `allowed_lemmas: []`, and every such candidate then fails `out_of_vocabulary`, because every lexical lemma in any text is outside the empty set. A text with no lexical lemma is not an escape: SpacyEsAdapter.analyse raises MissingInput on it. Every gap slot G4 emits was therefore UNFILLABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, in the code, independent of the corpus: the 918 slots of the 281b623 CI run and the 1,456 slots of the local 2,823-sentence run alike.
blocked.measured: 1,456 of 1,456 gap rows in build/es/g4/selected.jsonl carry an empty ledger. Probed with G5's own _axis: 'Hola.', '¿Qué?' and '¿Quién pregunta por mi hermana?' all return out_of_vocabulary against the real gap row u7/l37/s0.
blocked.beingFixedBy: p2fix-ledger-freeze, observed editing that branch to `new_lemmas = pending[:MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_EXERCISE]` and `known_lemmas = sorted(index.known - set(gap_new))`. This lane's window table below is computed against exactly that semantics.
blocked.rowContractIsAlsoInFlight: The row contract this lane was briefed with is being replaced while the lane is open. p2fix-ledger-freeze's working tree drops `allowed_lemmas` from G5's _AUTHORED_REQUIRED and puts `ledger_digest` in its place - 16 hex characters over the sorted `known | new` set, emitted per slot by a new `coursekit gaps <lang>` verb and copied onto every candidate. It also makes G5 read `content/<lang>/candidates/*.jsonl` in SORTED filename order (this lane's shard path is right) and turns `orphan_authored_slots` from a runlog note into a FAILED stage. So a shard authored before that lands would carry the wrong required key on every one of its 4,440 rows, and re-stamping it is not a text edit: the digest is derived from the frozen ledger, which is the thing that does not exist yet.

measuredFindingsForOtherLanes.finding: g5_gapfill._lemmas calls `analyser.analyse(text)` positionally, but SpacyEsAdapter.analyse is keyword-only: `analyse(self, *, sentence_id, text)`. G5 raises `TypeError: SpacyEsAdapter.analyse() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given` on the FIRST candidate it evaluates, before any axis verdict exists. G5 has never lemmatised an authored candidate.

Fixing the call convention is not enough. SpacyEsAdapter.analyse ends in `validate_record('analysed_sentence', ...)`, whose schema requires `sentence_id` to match ^[0-9a-f]{16}$. An authored candidate has no sentence id, so 'the same analyser that produced analysed_sentence for every corpus row' has no entry point for authored text at all. G5 needs either a lemmas-only method on the adapter contract or a synthetic content-addressed id; this lane's verifier uses sha256(text)[:16] as a stand-in and says so.

G3 resolves unit 21 (reflexive_verbs) to ONE target lemma. All 33 authored target_lexemes are reflexive infinitives (levantarse, ducharse, ...) and the pinned es_core_news_md lemmatises them without the clitic, so target_lexemes ∩ lexicon is empty and the unit falls back to ['que']. Unit 28 loses all six clitic pronouns (lo, me, te, nos, os, se) the same way. A unit that teaches one word is a V4 coverage failure waiting at the other end of the pipeline.
measuredFindingsForOtherLanes.reproduced: compare content/es/curriculum.yaml target_lexemes with build/es/g3/units.jsonl target_lemmas

measuredFindingsForOtherLanes.finding: The committed content/es/candidates.jsonl keys its 160 rows per-unit, e.g. (unit 2, lesson 1). G4's lesson_index is GLOBAL (unit 2 is lessons 7-12, unit 8 is 43-48), so none of its eight slots matches a gap row and the file fills nothing even after G4 is fixed. Slot keys: (1,1,0) (1,2,2) (2,1,1) (2,3,0) (3,1,4) (3,2,1) (4,1,0) (4,2,3).

G4 fails its own MAX_GAP_FRACTION=0.60 ceiling on the corpus this repo can actually assemble locally: 1,456/1,584 slots (92%) are gaps over 2,823 shippable Tatoeba sentences. The 281b623 CI run measured 918/1,584 (58%), just under the ceiling. The gap-slot LIST, and therefore this lane's 222-slot budget, moves with whatever corpus cap that lane freezes.

The four authoring lanes were started in parallel with the lane that defines what they author against. None of the three shard lanes can write a valid row until `coursekit gaps es` has been run against a G4 that carries the ledger, because BOTH halves of the stale_ledger axis (the digest and new_lemmas) are per-slot outputs of that build. Authoring is a dependent phase of the freeze, not a parallel one.

whatThisLaneCanHandOver.allowedLemmasAreCorpusIndependent: With p2fix-ledger-freeze's fix, a gap row's allowed set is `known_lemmas | new_lemmas` = `(index.known - gap_new) | gap_new` = **index.known**, and index.known is only ever grown by `index.introduce(chunk)` once per lesson and `index.introduce(target)` once per unit — both from G3's curriculum target_lemmas, never from a corpus sentence. So allowed_lemmas for EVERY slot of a lesson is one deterministic set, computable from build/es/g3/units.jsonl plus _split_new_lemmas, with no corpus at all. Only `new_lemmas` — one lemma per slot, off `pending` — depends on which slots the corpus filled, and that is the one thing the gap brief has to carry.
authoringConstraintsMeasuredAgainstThePi: Token count is len(tokens) from the adapter and tokens INCLUDE punctuation. '¿Cuál es tu apellido, por favor?' is 9 tokens, not 6. A question costs two tokens (¿ and ?) before a word is written, so the 3-12 window is tighter than it reads.
Lemmas are the LEXICAL tokens only (PUNCT/SYM/SPACE/X are dropped), so punctuation never has to be in allowed_lemmas.
'un' and 'una' lemmatise to 'uno', which is in the window from unit 2's numbers. Indefinite articles are usable from unit 7 even though 'un' is not a target lexeme until unit 30.
Not in the unit-7 window and commonly reached for: 'estar', 'que' (unit 21), 'a' (never a target lexeme), 'se', 'hacer', 'ir', 'muy', 'este'. No relative clauses and no personal 'a' before unit 21.
whatThisLaneCanHandOver.verifier: scratchpad/verify_shard.py reproduces G5's REJECT_AXES order over a shard against a gap brief, reading G5's own constants (MIN_TOKENS, MAX_TOKENS, MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_ITEM, MIN_CANDIDATES_PER_SLOT, AUTHORED_PROVENANCE, _AUTHORED_REQUIRED, Slot) so it cannot drift from the stage. It reports filled/unfilled/thin/orphan slots, the per-axis reject counts, and the backtranslation score distribution, and it FAILS on a uniform-4 score file's shape by printing the distribution rather than a pass.
whatThisLaneCanHandOver.pilotVerified: 24 unit-7 lesson-37 question-word candidates were authored and run through the pinned es_core_news_md against the computed 198-lemma window: 23 pass the vocabulary and 3-12 token axes, 1 rejects (`primos` is left unlemmatised by the pinned model, so a plural that is in the window as `primo` is out of vocabulary as `primos`). That is the method working end to end on real output, and the one reject is a lemmatiser quirk every authoring lane will hit and should check for rather than assume.

lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.$comment: Every one of these is a form whose LEMMA is not the window entry an author would expect, measured by running the pinned es_core_news_md over authored candidates. Each one costs a candidate on the out_of_vocabulary axis and none of them is visible by reading the window list. An authoring lane should run its texts through the analyser before it writes translations for them, not after.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.primos: stays 'primos'. 'primo' is in the window; the plural is not lemmatised to it.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.cuántas: lemmatises to 'cuántos', not 'cuánto'. The window carries 'cuánto', so every '¿Cuántas ...?' is out of vocabulary.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.ninguna: lemmatises to 'ninguno', which is in no unit's target list.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.ayudo: first person singular stays 'ayudo' in some contexts rather than 'ayudar'.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.disculpe / disculpa: stay as the surface form; 'disculpar' is in the window and is never reached from the imperative.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.un / una: DO lemmatise to 'uno', which IS in the window from unit 2. Indefinite articles are usable.
lemmatiserTrapsMeasuredNotAssumed.a: the preposition is in no unit's target_lexemes anywhere in the course, so the personal 'a' ('¿Conoces a mi hermana?') can never be authored. 'que' arrives only at unit 21, so no relative clauses either.

pilotBank.where: scratchpad/bank/l37..l42.txt, the six lessons of unit 7 (the unit that was 100% gaps at 281b623: 54 of 54 slots)
pilotBank.note: Texts only. They are NOT committed as candidates, because a candidate needs the slot's ledger_digest and new_lemmas, and both are outputs of a build that has not run. The 9.7% that reject are the trap table above, which is the reason a text bank has to be analysed before it is dressed as a row.

whatThisLaneCanHandOver.ledgerFixVerifiedAgainstThePrecomputedWi: p2fix-ledger-freeze's in-progress g4_select.py was run in a scratchpad copy of the package against this worktree's build. Before it, 1,456 of 1,456 gap rows carried an empty ledger. After it, 0 do, and the emitted `known | new` set EQUALS this lane's precomputed window on every gap row — 1,339 of 1,339 on the first run and 490 of 490 on a rebuilt one, zero mismatches either time. The claim that allowed_lemmas is computable without a corpus is therefore measured, not argued. G2's resolution of units 1-7 was also identical across two independent runs (unit 1 loses gracias/ella/nosotros/ellos/llamarse, unit 4 loses cuchara, units 2/3/5/6/7 lose nothing), so the lesson-37 window of 198 lemmas is reproducible.

verification.note: The verifier still reports FAIL overall, correctly: the other 122 gap slots of units 7-14 in that build have no candidates. FAIL is the honest verdict for a shard that covers one lesson.

shardState.whyOnlyLesson37: Every row needs the slot's new_lemmas, and G4 draws those from `pending` — the unit's target lemmas not yet SHOWN. A filled slot consumes pending lemmas in a corpus-dependent way, so for a unit that is only partly gaps the per-slot new lemma cannot be known without the frozen build. Unit 7 is the exception: it is 100% gaps (54 of 54 slots) in the 281b623 CI measurement and in all three local runs, and a unit's own target lemmas can never be in `shown` before that unit, so its pending walk is deterministic. Lesson 37 was authored against that determinism: slots 0-5 take qué, quién, cuál, cuándo, porque, para in curriculum order and slots 6-8 take none, which is exactly what the patched G4 emits.
shardState.eachRowCarriesBothContracts: allowed_lemmas (the contract as committed) AND ledger_digest (the contract landing in p2fix-ledger-freeze), so the shard is readable under either. If the frozen build's corpus cap moves G2's lexicon, the window moves, the digest moves with it, and these rows fail by name on the stale_ledger axis rather than filling a slot they no longer fit.
